identity.real_world_identity_notes: Lola T95/00 of the 1995 IndyCar season, a chassis raced with Ford/Cosworth XB and Mercedes-Benz IC108 engines among others, fitted with a six-speed manual gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts, no automatic blip, and a clutch needed to pull away, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.

This class runs three configurations rather than two: base, high downforce and Speedway. Speedway is an oval package, which is why the suffix differs from the downforce pairs used elsewhere in the dataset.
This car was observed in all three of the class's configurations, so it anchors the identity format for the others.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.lola-t95-00-ford-cosworth-high-downforce.20260815t215804247z-ea474fd1 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the chassis and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a six-speed gearbox for this chassis, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick with automatic cut and no automatic blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Turbocharged Champ Car with a sequential stick. The car cuts the upshift, so keep it flat and pull the next gear. Nothing blips for you, so match the revs on every downshift: these are light, powerful, rear-drive cars and an unmatched downshift steps the back out.
